correctness.rationale: For n<=floor(1/phi)+1 all nodes remain one-exposure vulnerable after insertion, so connectivity forces full adoption both ways. For phi>1/2 a single seed only activates immediate degree-one neighbors, and one edge changes at most two of these statuses; a leaf-to-leaf tie in a star attains loss two. For phi<=1/2 a tree with gateway degree k=floor(1/phi) and trailing degree-two path fully adopts, while closing one chord from gateway to path endpoint raises gateway degree to k+1 and permanently prevents every additional adopter; loss n-1 is absolute maximum. Endpoint inequalities 1/(k+1)<phi<=1/k and phi<=1/2 are exact. Verification executable uses Fraction arithmetic for 128360 upper-bound checks and 64 construction checks. This computation is supplementary to proof.

originality.rationale: The universal finite-network tie-insertion loss classification, including the sharp smallest order and two-versus-unbounded half-threshold boundary, is not stated by the inspected Watts, Whitney, Singh or Easley–Kleinberg accounts. Searches for precise graph-pair extremal formulas, equivalent degree-dilution terminology and stronger coverage identified no directly dominating theorem. Local one-neighbor vulnerability and dense-cluster cascade criteria are acknowledged pre-existing ingredients, not claimed as discoveries. Broader previously published graph-extremal findings remain an unresolved historical-priority risk.

value.rationale: The worst-case loss of adoption under adding one tie is an intrinsic, directly motivated social-network robustness invariant. The classification has a sharp minimum network order and a true discontinuity of extremal behavior at one-half: bounded loss of two above it versus arbitrarily many lost adopters below, even when the original network fully adopts. It resolves an all-graph all-threshold sensitivity question rather than a hand-picked small case. Model-specific idealizations and typical-case irrelevance are expressly limited.
